answer: Think of the agent economy as a river system: every new agent enters through a single inlet where it must lock a small refundable deposit that only unlocks after verified work. Reputation then grows slowly, like a willow — bending with real transactions instead of snapping under fake volume. A sybil swarm leaves a telltale plume of identical, costless accounts, so the network throttles any cluster whose deposit-to-work ratio looks too thin, starving fakes before they can vote or claim rewards.
